abstract: Tier-1 individual-level predictions for the Silicon Sample Benchmark. This is the secondary-1 entry of a matched pair; it differs from our primary entry by exactly one factor, how the multi-item scales are asked. A synthetic panel of 9,000 respondents is built by raking the post-stratification weights of 9,000 General Social Survey respondents onto the preregistered quota margins, then quota-sampling within each of the 17 conditions, so demographic composition is not a confound of the treatment effects. Each respondent is assigned one condition (500 per intervention, 1,000 in control, one of the three filler texts for each control respondent) and is rendered as a fixed-template persona sentence built in code, with no second model. Survey administration is hybrid. The 37 items of the 6 multi-item outcomes are asked as blocks: every item of one scale is on one page and is answered by a local open-weights model in one forward pass, under a regex that constrains the answer shape but never its value, at temperature 1.6. The 7 single-item outcomes are asked one item per call and their values are reused unchanged from the primary entry, not regenerated. Block prompting raises the mean inter-item correlation on the 12-item trust scale from 0.10 in the primary entry to 0.84, against about 0.53 for real people on the identical scale; it also narrows each single answer and nearly removes extreme responses. Both effects are measured and reported in the registration form, and no value was adjusted after any diagnostic was read. The 6 composite outcomes are built by the benchmark's own scripts/clean.R from the raw items, never in our code. No human outcome data from this study, or from any pilot of it, informed any part of the pipeline.
approach_family: per-respondent simulation; GSS-based quota-matched synthetic panel of 9,000; fixed-template persona rendering, no persona-writing model; one local open-weights model answers every survey item for each respondent; hybrid survey administration - block prompting with regex-constrained structured output for the 6 multi-item outcomes (37 items, one prompt per scale, temperature 1.6), item-level prompting for the 7 single-item outcomes (reused unchanged from our primary entry); composites computed by the benchmark's own scripts/clean.R; zero-shot
